subject: Business Models
title: Product-as-a-Service
description: A micro-lesson that makes Product-as-a-Service usable.

hook.text: Michelin sells 'tires-as-a-service' to trucking companies. Pay per mile driven, not per tire purchased.

buildup.text: Product-as-a-service transforms purchases into ongoing services: pay for use, not ownership.

discovery.text: Michelin maintains and replaces tires itself, ensuring optimal performance. It profits when tires last longer.

twist.text: This flips the incentive: manufacturers benefit from durability, not planned obsolescence. Longer life = more profit.

climax.text: Product-as-a-service aligns manufacturer incentives with sustainability. It's profitable and environmentally sound.

punchline.text: Pay per mile, not per tire. When durability profits, sustainability follows.

quiz.question: How does product-as-a-service change manufacturer incentives?
options: They profit from durability instead of planned obsolescence
